oracle: CUDA target-gather on production matrix plus exact CPU record oracle on the Gate-0 small matrix

performance.steady_definition: source upload plus dense-scatter kernel; frame-local A/B remains device-resident

implementation_evidence.clip_implementation: four-plane Sutherland-Hodgman with ping-pong vertex buffers
implementation_evidence.atomic_repeatability_scope: two consecutive dense-scatter runs for every matrix case
implementation_evidence.test_result: All tests passed: 314 assertions in one hidden Gate-1 case

selection_rationale: Dense scatter passed every predeclared correctness, support, flux, repeatability and performance threshold.
Dense scatter creates no host contribution records and uses memory independent of frame count for frame-local A/B planes.
Target gather remains the production-size correctness oracle but was slower in every measured matrix case.
The selected scatter workspace uses no cudaDeviceSynchronize and performs no buffer allocation in the per-frame hotpath.
limitations_carried_forward: Double atomicAdd repeatability is demonstrated on the frozen GTX 1660 Ti matrix, not proven for every future GPU architecture.
Three stream synchronizations remain for separated Gate-1 timing; Gate 6 must overlap upload, compute and downstream device reduction.
Full frame-local A/B downloads are correctness-only and must not occur per frame in the selected production pipeline.
Gate 1 selects affine enumeration only. Robust reduction, support/fold, confidence, memory/I/O, transaction and local warp gates remain open.
